title: Compact playbook delta serializer and rate-limited snapshotter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce compact delta serializer for playbook snapshots and a rate-limited snapshotter to reduce telemetry pressure during noisy incidents. Feature-flagged and backward-compatible; rollout to 10% of oncall hubs initially.
body:
Context: On-call clients and the handoff service currently store full playbook snapshots whenever a responder adds a step or an annotation. During large incidents this produces heavy telemetry and storage churn (noise) and makes diffs hard to surface in the UI. This PR introduces a compact delta serializer for playbook snapshots and a rate-limited snapshotter that reduces redundant writes while preserving deterministic reconstruction for handoffs and audit logs.

Design summary: single continuous description below. Compact delta serializer: a new serializer that stores only operational deltas (add-step, edit-step, resolve-step, meta-update) instead of full JSON blobs. Deltas are canonicalized and optionally gzipped; we use a short op-code schema to minimize per-delta size. Rate-limited snapshotter: client-side and server-side rate limiter with a leaky-bucket implementation to cap snapshot writes to the store under noisy activity. A debounced flush triggers when the bucket has capacity or when an incident reaches stable states (acknowledged/resolved).

Compatibility and safety: All deltas are reversible; the playbook store includes a compatibility layer that can apply deltas to the latest full baseline. We keep periodic full checkpoints (configurable; default 24h or 1 full checkpoint per 100 deltas) so reconstruction cost is bounded. This change is guarded by the feature flag slo.compact_playbook_deltas and a server-side rollout percentage.

Operational impacts: Expected storage reduction of 3–6x in noisy incidents based on experiment data. Snapshot write rate to the canonical store will be rate-limited by default to 10 writes/min per playbook instance during high-churn windows, configurable by org. Audit logging still records operations (op-code + actor + timestamp) with a pointer to the delta blob.

Checklist:
- [x] Serializer implementation and unit tests
- [x] Client-side rate limiter + integration tests
- [x] Server-side acceptor and migration path for existing full-blobs
- [x] Feature flag + rollout plan
- [x] Docs + public API change notes
- [x] Performance benchmarks and end-to-end smoke tests

Testing: Local unit+integration test suites cover serialization round-trip, delta application ordering, and conflict windows (concurrent edits). Added a lightweight stress harness that simulates 1k events/min across 50 playbooks; storage usage reduced ~4.1x and median snapshot latency remained within SLOs. CI runs included the new stress unit as a part of the integration suite.

Rollout plan: Feature flag off by default. Step 1: enable for internal staging (done). Step 2: enable for 10% of production oncall hubs for 72h while monitoring snapshot-write-rate and reconstruction error (metrics added: playbook.delta_bytes, playbook.snapshot_writes, playbook.reconstruction_failures). Step 3: ramp to 50% then 100% if no regressions. On detection of any reconstruction failures the system falls back to full snapshot mode automatically for affected playbooks and alerts the SRE runbook.

Notes: This PR focuses purely on the serialization and rate-limiter; a follow-up will add UI diff summarizer logic to render compact deltas in the handoff timeline.

review_comments: Ethan Collins (2026-02-20): Nice approach. Two asks: 1) please add a sanity-check that prevents deltas older than the last checkpoint from being applied if they arrive out-of-order; 2) confirm the gzipping threshold (I think 512 bytes).

Maya Patel (author) reply (2026-02-21): Added the ordering guard in applyDelta() and made gzip threshold configurable with default 512 bytes. See serializer/compact_delta.go lines handling compressThreshold.
Liu Zhang (2026-02-23): The migration importer should run with a rate limit to avoid saturating storage. Can we make it chunked and add progress logging?
Maya Patel reply (2026-02-24): Migration importer now streams in 1k-playbook batches with a 200ms pause between batches; progress is emitted to logs and the tool supports dry-run mode. Tests updated.
Priya Menon (2026-02-26): CI integration looks flaky on macos runner — the stress test relies on PRNG seeding for deterministic timing. Please make timing tolerant and add a retry on flakey assert.
Maya Patel reply (2026-02-27): Reworked test harness to use wall-clock windows and added a flaky-assert retry decorator; CI green on repeated runs.
